thread:
incident-bot: PagerDuty alert triggered — p99 generation latency > 2.5s for canary v6 across us-west-2. Auto-inserted page to #incidents.
nya: I’m on it, grabbing context. Paging SREs.
alex: Observing a clear step-up in tail latency starting at 1901234000, correlated with the v6 canary traffic shift (10% -> 30%). p95 up ~30%, p99 up ~3–4x.
maria: Any streaming stalls or just generation latency?
alex: Both. Streaming stalls visible on sessions with >512 tokens. We’re seeing stalled async writes to the client — likely backend token emit backlog.
chen: Dumping recent kube events and pod logs now. Suspect KV cache thrash on the new attention kernel in v6.
jordan: Customer impact? Which customers hit canary?
alex: Mostly internal smoke + three SaaS customers on alpha flag (cs-42, cs-77, cs-omega). Support notified.
support-bot: Notified customer success and created ticket CS-8729 for cs-42 and cs-77. CS-omega on call.
nya: OK mitigation options: 1) Shift canary back to 10% immediately, 2) Scale up inference pool for canary workers (adds cost, quick), 3) Rollback v6 entirely. Prefer fast mitigation to reduce customer impact.
kevin: Can we do traffic steering to v5 only for streaming endpoints and keep v6 for non-streaming? That isolates the streaming regression.
chen: Technically doable: route-by-capability rule. But config change needs to push and will take ~2–3min + warmup.
maria: How fast is scale up? We have spare nodes in us-west-2; can autoscale add nodes in ~90s?
jordan: If we scale, the p99 drops a bit but tail still elevated — looks like a kernel-level stall not pure capacity.
alex: I captured a couple of stack traces from a stalled worker: 
```
[worker-1234] wait_for_kv_cache: blocking on shm->lock for 2800ms
model_attention_kernel::compute_chunk() stuck in memcpy with intermittent 100ms stalls
```
This points to shared memory contention on the KV store when sequence lengths increase.
nya: Given that, traffic shift back to 10% + isolate streaming route to v5 sounds safest. We should avoid full rollback unless the partial mitigations fail.
support-bot: Escalated to AE for cs-omega; they reported slow streaming responses and some timing out at ~8s.
kevin: I’ll prepare a routing override: send streaming-based requests (has_streaming=true) to v5 for the next 30m. Pushing policy now.
(kevin) pushed routing override: setting route "streaming_capable=true -> v5" (deploy id rv-2026).
maria: Watch metrics for 2 minutes after policy takes effect.
alex: After route change: p95 back to 220ms, p99 improved to ~1.1s for streaming; non-streaming v6 p99 still ~2.4s at 30% traffic.
chen: Rolling cache warmups on v6 instances show same shm contention on long sequences. Need code-level fix in kernel or fallback to older attention path.
jordan: Customers—cs-42 and cs-77 report improvements on streaming path; cs-omega still sees occasional non-streaming slowness (they hit batch endpoints). Support pinged.
nya: Good. Action items: 
- kevin: keep streaming route override for 30m, then evaluate extension.
- chen: bisect v6 to identify offending commit and test fallback kernel.
- alex/maria: monitor p95/p99, add dashboard annotations at 1901234567 for the event.
- support-bot: maintain customer comms and note mitigation steps in CS tickets.
kevin: Confirmed override active. Tagging the rollout as partial rollback for streaming traffic.
(5m later) alex: p99 for canary overall down 45%, streaming fully recovered. Non-streaming tail still elevated but no new customer timeouts reported.
maria: If chen’s bisect finds a quick revert candidate we can do a targeted rollback of the kernel change. Otherwise schedule full rollback during the 22:00 maintenance window.
chen: I found a commit that introduced a lock around the shared KV update for chunked attention (commit c3f9b2). Repro locally with long sequences. Working on a patch to reduce lock contention by sharding the KV writes.
jordan: Customer impact summary for ops notes: brief service degradation for three alpha customers, streaming endpoints affected; mitigated by routing override; no billing adjustments requested yet.
support-bot: CS tickets updated with mitigation and ETA for permanent fix.
nya: Handoff to evening oncall @alex at 1901234700. If override fails extend to 2h and prepare rollback runbook.
alex: Acknowledged handoff. Will keep exec updates minimal unless customer escalations.
(incident-bot) Incident severity: SEV3 -> downgraded to SEV4 after mitigation at 1901234750.
kevin: Leaving override in place until chen’s patch is validated in staging.
chen: Patch pushed to staging branch; running canary with v6+patch at 10% now. Early signs: no shm stalls in trace. Will validate over 30m.
maria: Great. Closing notes: add postmortem placeholders, timeline, and suggested mitigation (routing-by-capability + shard KV writes).
nya: Thanks team. If anything else pops, re-open thread. :thumbsup:
